questions.question: Why can asynchronous replication lose committed data on failover?
options: The source replies to the client before any replica has the transaction
questions.explanation: With async replication, transactions may exist only on the failed primary, so promoting a replica gives an RPO above zero.

questions.question: A 5-member Group Replication group loses contact with 2 members. Can the remaining 3 keep accepting writes?
options: No, all members must be reachable
No, a group needs at least 4 members
questions.explanation: A group needs a majority; 5 members tolerate 2 failures, and the majority is 3.

questions.question: In an InnoDB Cluster, what does the application connect to?
options: MySQL Router, which routes to the current primary
questions.explanation: Router learns the topology from cluster metadata and sends read-write connections to the primary, including after a failover.

questions.question: Why is a 2-member Group Replication group pointless for HA?
options: Group Replication needs at least 9 members
Losing either member loses the majority, so quorum is gone
Single-primary mode requires three nodes for backups
questions.explanation: With 2 members the majority is 2, so no failures are tolerated.
